experiments.question: Which booking-api@v1 fixtures can simple-login.integration replay exactly through the dev proxy against the real service on the real clock and a database whose bookings it does not fix (Q-069 counted 14)?
experiments.finding: 15 of 35: the eight 400 VALIDATION_FAILED, the four 401 UNAUTHORIZED (my-bookings-expired-token through the restart), cancel-unknown and cancel-malformed-id (404), and book-too-long (422 BOOKING_TOO_LONG, order 3 of POST, before the clock's orders 4 and 5). A reference model of the check orders gave each the same answer under 7 clocks from 2026-11-01 to 2028-11-01 and two stored states (none; 78,912 random-id bookings); the other 20 changed under at least one.

experiments.question: Can the browser tests book on both the next last Sunday of March and of October after the real clock within booking-api@v1's 365 days, and which strings will those bookings show?
experiments.finding: Scanning every hour from 2026-11-01 to 2032, the nearer change day's planned booking is at most 217.02 days ahead; the farther one is beyond 365 days only for about six days in some years (2029-03-25 to 03-31, 2031-10-25 to 11-01). From 2026-11-01 both 2027-03-28 (147 days, 23 h, 92 quarter hours, no 01:xx) and 2027-10-31 (364 days, 25 h, 100, 01:00 to 01:45 BST then GMT) are bookable. budi sees '00:30 to 02:30' and '01:30 BST to 01:30 GMT'; ayu sees '07:30 to 08:30' then '(00:30 to 02:30 in London)' and '(01:30 BST to 01:30 GMT in London)'; budi's Home lines 'Sun 28 Mar  00:30 to 02:30' and 'Sun 31 Oct  01:30 BST to 01:30 GMT'.

experiments.question: In the installed Chrome under Playwright 1.64.1, does a context's timezoneId set the page's ambient zone, and does page.clock.setFixedTime hold only the browser's clock behind the real one while timers run (for the AC-5.5 browser test)?
experiments.finding: Yes to both: timezoneId Asia/Kolkata gives the page Asia/Calcutta, offset -330, 02:00Z at hour 7; setFixedTime five minutes before the current quarter hour, set before goto, holds Date.now() and new Date() at that instant while setInterval still fires (19 ticks a second), and the test process keeps the real clock. The current quarter hour was after the page's clock and already started on the real one.

routed.text: From S20 (simple-login.integration's PRD v2 append, DEC-182, DEC-183). simple-login.integration.3 starts the service with `npm --prefix backend start`, PORT=3000 and DATABASE_URL=postgres://meeting_rooms:meeting_rooms@127.0.0.1:55432/meeting_rooms_e2e, a database its Playwright global setup has just dropped and re-created through the `pg` package on the backend's Compose service, and assumes the service creates its tables and the four pre-loaded rooms in that empty database at start. The integration plan's pending section asks this as a request on booking-api@v1; if the answer is a separate command, the integration's global setup runs it with the same DATABASE_URL. The rig never names a path under backend/ any more.

From S20. The shipped integration rig (simple-login.integration.1 and .2) spawns backend/src/server.ts directly with PORT=3000, no `db:up` and no DATABASE_URL. From the backend phase that makes the service need PostgreSQL until simple-login.integration.3 merges, the root `npm test` passes only while an earlier step (the backend's gate or replay) has left PostgreSQL running; simple-login.integration.3's Dependencies say to land it with that work.

closes.note: The appended phases consume auth-api@v1, profile-api@v2 and booking-api@v1; none cites profile-api@v1. The citations of profile-api@v1 in the header's Consumes and in simple-login.integration.1 and .2 are shipped history and stay; the confirm entries name only the appended phases, and profile-api@v1's deprecation stays with C-1 and Sync A.

The Sources entry for hsdd/context/prd-simple-login.v2.md keeps its six sections and gains US-1, AC-2.2, AC-2.3, AC-2.5, US-3, US-4, US-5, US-6, Rooms and Screens, which covers AC-4.4, AC-5.5 and AC-6.2 (DEC-194). H19's version ripple copies it into the root's embedded summary.

The restart stays the AC-2.3 expired-token stand-in (ADR-001 keeps sessions in memory). simple-login.integration.3's restart test sees each old token answer 401 and signs in again before listing the bookings; .4's browser version does the same through Login.

The browser runs in Asia/Kolkata (DEC-191); the change-day tests take the next last Sunday of March and of October strictly after today's date in London and book where booking-api@v1's 365 days allow (DEC-189); the started cases are named (DEC-187); ADR-002 Decision 7's strings, including '23:00 to Fri 6 Nov 02:00' and '01:30 BST'/'01:30 GMT', are in .4's and .5's Scope.

The 365-day horizon keeps the nearer change day bookable (at most 217.02 days, experiment integration-clock-change-days); 20 simultaneous attempts give one 201 and nineteen 409 naming the winner (DEC-186); the restart test signs in again and finds every booking with its id. The proxy replay takes 15 booking-api@v1 fixtures, not 14: book-too-long also answers before any clock or state rule (DEC-185). The confirm entry names simple-login.integration.3, .4 and .5 as consumers.
simple-login.integration.3's Scope cites auth-api@v1 G3 for the restart (every token ends, bookings stay) and booking-api@v1 G17; sign-out stays client-side (G4), so no test calls a logout endpoint.

simple-login.integration.4's AC-2.5 test reads each account's zone from profile-api@v2's me-ayu and me-budi fixtures; .3's Dependencies record that the shipped replay of those two fixtures fails until simple-login.backend.4 serves timeZone.
simple-login.integration.4 drops the 3-second assertion from e2e/login.spec.ts; the AC-1.1 test asserts AC-1.1 only (DEC-188). No line names the 3 seconds as a PRD criterion.

Each browser run uses a database of its own, meeting_rooms_e2e, re-created through `pg` on the backend's Compose service, never the backend's tables (DEC-182); the Playwright config sets the Asia/Kolkata zone and the service runs on the real clock; the started booking is the backend's replay's (DEC-187), and booking a started time is tested at the service and, with only the browser's clock held back, in the browser.

The root scripts and the global setup start PostgreSQL only with `npm --prefix backend run db:up`, never `docker compose` (DEC-184); the service starts with `npm --prefix backend start` after it (DEC-183); the tests set DATABASE_URL to meeting_rooms_e2e and never write meeting_rooms; booking-api@v1's producer simple-login.backend.7 is .3's dependency.

simple-login.integration.4 and .5 select by the visible strings listed (Time zone, My bookings, Cancel, (no bookings), Book a room, Rooms on, Home, room/start/end/title, Book) and assert the messages ('Booked.', AC-5.3's sentence, 'That time has already started.', the AC-2.3 message after a 401 at a booking call); a started-time refusal through the UI holds the browser's clock back, since the form leaves passed starts out.
